Kit

Integration-test your game

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Process launch and log assertionsHarness referenceGenerated probesWriting assertions

Use the template's integration harness to check multiplayer behavior across processes using the game's network transport. Installed addons include harness.sh and a driver.gd skeleton in addons/odin_godot/template/test/. Repository examples source the same harness from build/template/test/harness.sh in build/template/test/. Scriptgen generates probes that let the driver inspect replicated state.

examples/cavecrawl/run.sh demonstrates four scenarios: story progression, save/resume, match flow with moderation, and host migration after kill -9. Each uses the shared harness for launch, synchronization, and log assertions.

For framework contributors, tests/wireabi/run.sh is the protocol-layout fixture. It generates one nested schema, executes its exact raw byte vector natively, and compiles the same fingerprint/layout assertions for web, Linux, and Windows targets. The native pass queries the generated NET_SCHEMA field, action, argument, type, and message tables; a profile-only package pins that projection too, while tests/repgen covers inputs, constraints, entity ids, scheduled actions, and presentation events. The fixture also proves a schema drift is denied by the real JOIN handshake and pins recursive diagnostics across replicated fields, input records, profiles, and typed messages, including platform-width integers, implicit enums, pointers, hidden padding, and unsupported containers.

tests/author_surface/run.sh guards the authoring language itself. It compiles negative fixtures for removed event attributes, quoted command policies, and redundant owner interpolation, then scans production source for retired action aliases and ID-only census generation. A compatibility spelling cannot return without making the complete suite fail.

tests/kitdocs/run.sh guards the prose around that language. It verifies every relative link in docs/kit, rejects retired symbols, and prevents tutorial pages from teaching raw session lifecycle or _net_pump as the ordinary path.

tests/kitstress/run.sh is the optimized scale/operations gate. It prints three receipts:

  • STRESS: delta CPU at 0/10/100% dirty, join/world/snapshot bytes, apply and resume CPU, and session resident/peak allocation for 100/500/2,000 entities.
  • FANOUT: per-recipient AOI composition CPU and authority egress at 2/100, 4/500, and 8/2,000 player/entity shapes.
  • RESIM: forced eight-tick replay CPU and prediction-history bytes for 32/128/512 predicted entities.

The generous timing assertions detect complexity regressions, not machine speed. The supported starting values derived from these fixtures live in network_profile_envelope; profiles explains what they do and do not guarantee.

Process launch and log assertions#

Launch N headless processes of the main game scene. Use netgd's link shim with *_LATENCY / *_JITTER / *_LOSS environment variables to inject delay, jitter, and packet loss. A GDScript SceneTree driver calls the same @(gd_method) procedures as the UI and prints an uppercase log tag for each observable result. The scenario exercises the scene and transport without mocking them. In run.sh, source the harness, wrap each scenario in an act, and check its logs:

Shell
source addons/odin_godot/template/test/harness.sh
fslp_build

duel() {                                  # one act: a self-contained scenario
    local port="$1"
    local hlog="$FSLP_LOGS/h.log" glog="$FSLP_LOGS/g.log"
    local hp gp
    hp=$(fslp_launch host "$hlog" MYGAME_PORT="$port")
    fslp_ready "$hlog" "HOSTING" 10 "$hp" || return 1     # bind receipt or retry
    gp=$(fslp_launch guest "$glog" MYGAME_PORT="$port" MYGAME_LATENCY=120)
    fslp_wait_all 90 "$hp" "$gp"
    expect       "$hlog" "GAME_STARTED"                "the round never started"
    expect_same  "$hlog" "$glog" "SCATTER sum=[0-9]+"  "the worlds diverged"
    expect_count "$glog" "WAVE_CLEARED" 2              "the guest cleared both waves"
    expect_absent "$hlog" "_FAIL"                      "the host driver failed"
}

fslp_act "the duel" 3 duel     # 3 tries, fresh port each — bind races retry
fslp_verdict MYGAME            # MYGAME_OK / MYGAME_FAIL

Harness reference#

  • fslp_act NAME TRIES FN retries an act on fresh ports. A bind conflict consumes one try. Exhausting retries fails the run, but later acts still execute so their results are also reported.
  • fslp_ready LOG PATTERN SECS PID waits for the expected log receipt before launching the next peer. It fails early if the process exits, such as when its port is already in use.
  • fslp_wait_all SECS PIDS... waits for drivers to print ROLE_DONE/ROLE_FAIL and exit, then reaps any remaining processes after the deadline.
  • fslp_reap [PIDS...] sends TERM, allows stdout to flush, then sends -9. An immediate kill -9 can truncate buffered logs. Use kill -9 directly when testing a crash, as Cavecrawl's migration act does to its host.
  • expect / expect_same / expect_absent / expect_count update FSLP_OK with assertion results. Custom grep checks can update the same value for assertions spanning logs or requiring other count rules.

Generated probes#

For each entity= kind, scriptgen registers @(gd_method) probes on the game class to read counts, local ownership, and replicated scalar fields:

Code
probe_<kind>_count()           # live entities of the kind, as this peer sees it
probe_my_<kind>()              # my entity's net id (0 = none)
probe_<kind>_<field>(id)       # any replicated SCALAR field; id 0 = mine

For example, game.probe_kicker_hp(0) in driver.gd reads this peer's local entity hp through a generated method. Probes read the replicated fields used for presentation; in a simulation game, those fields contain presentation values after lane_present. Add game-specific probes for derived values such as a predicted-hp overlay, a nearest-entity search, or formatted compound data. A hand-written procedure with a probe's name suppresses that generated probe.

Writing assertions#

  • Read verdicts from logs. The launch subshell owns the process ids, so drivers report ROLE_DONE / ROLE_FAIL for the harness to check.
  • Check each expected observer. Assert an event on every peer that should receive it. Use expect_same for byte-identical seeds, checksums, or blob contents when determinism matters.
  • Use the identity the session assigned. With simultaneous joins, which peer becomes player 2 depends on arrival order. Drivers that inspect their assigned role and assertions over combined logs can handle either order.
  • Hold state long enough to observe it. A flag set and cleared within one polling interval may never be read. Allow for both the slowest driver poll and delayed presentation; see "The two timelines" in net.md.
  • Use ranges for changing remote fields. An exact hp assertion during regeneration can race an update. Check a range or assert a logged value from the process that computed it.
  • Test above 100ms. Localhost can hide prediction, change-order, and presentation problems. Reference tests inject 120ms+ delay. Add jitter and loss cases too; delay alone does not exercise irregular or missing packets.
